content: The Pneumococcal Vaccine 13-Valent (PCV13) is a vaccine approved by the FDA for the prevention of infections caused by specific serotypes of Streptococcus pneumoniae. It is indicated for use in children aged 6 weeks to 17 years and adults aged 50 years and older. The vaccine targets 13 serotypes: 1, 3, 4, 5, 6A, 6B, 7F, 9V, 14, 18C, 19A, 19F, and 23F. Administration Instructions: The vaccine is a suspension containing an adjuvant. It must be shaken vigorously before use to ensure a homogeneous, white suspension. If the vaccine cannot be resuspended, it should not be used. Parenteral drug products should be visually inspected for particulate matter and discoloration before administration. If either is present, the vaccine should not be used. PCV13 is for intramuscular injection only. A 0.5 mL dose is administered using a sterile needle attached to the supplied prefilled syringe. Preferred injection sites include the anterolateral aspect of the thigh in infants and the deltoid muscle of the upper arm in toddlers, children, and adults. The vaccine should not be injected into the gluteal area or areas near major nerve trunks or blood vessels. PCV13 should not be mixed with other vaccines or products in the same syringe. Pediatric Dosage: For infants, the vaccine is administered as a four-dose series at 2, 4, 6, and 12–15 months of age. For children aged 7 months to 5 years who have not received PCV13, a catch-up schedule is recommended. However, the immune response may result in lower antibody concentrations for some serotypes compared to the standard four-dose series. Children aged 15 months to 5 years who are fully immunized with the 7-valent pneumococcal vaccine (PCV7) may receive one dose of PCV13 to elicit immune responses to the six additional serotypes. This supplemental dose should be administered at least 8 weeks after the final dose of PCV7. For children aged 6 to 17 years, PCV13 is administered as a single dose. If PCV7 was previously administered, at least 8 weeks should elapse before receiving PCV13. Adult Dosage: PCV13 is administered as a single dose for adults aged 50 years and older. The vaccine should not be mixed with other vaccines in the same syringe. Warnings and Precautions: Epinephrine and other agents for managing immediate allergic reactions must be readily available in case of an acute anaphylactic reaction following administration. Individuals with conditions such as congenital or acquired splenic dysfunction, HIV infection, malignancy, hematopoietic stem cell transplant, or nephrotic syndrome may have reduced antibody responses to PCV13. Apnea has been observed following intramuscular vaccination in some prematurely born infants. Decisions regarding vaccination in this population should consider the infant's medical status and the potential benefits and risks of vaccination. Adverse Reactions: Common adverse reactions include redness, swelling, and pain at the injection site, as well as systemic reactions such as fatigue, headache, decreased appetite, myalgia, arthralgia, and irritability. In clinical trials, diarrhea, vomiting, and rash occurred in more than 1% of infants and toddlers. Less common reactions (<1%) included hypersensitivity reactions (e.g., facial edema, dyspnea, bronchospasm), febrile seizures, and urticaria. Serious adverse events were reported at similar rates between PCV13 and PCV7 recipients in clinical trials. Postmarketing Experience: Adverse events reported through passive surveillance include vaccination-site dermatitis, pruritus, and urticaria; localized lymphadenopathy; cyanosis; anaphylactic reactions; hypotonia; angioneurotic edema; erythema multiforme; apnea; and pallor. These events are based on severity, frequency of reporting, or evidence of a causal relationship to PCV13. Drug Interactions: PCV13 has been administered concomitantly with other U.S.-licensed vaccines, such as DTaP-HBV-IPV, Hib, MMR, varicella, and hepatitis A vaccines, in infants and toddlers. However, data are insufficient to assess concomitant administration with HPV, meningococcal conjugate vaccine, or Tdap in children and adolescents. In adults, PCV13 has been administered concomitantly with trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine (TIV). When administered with other injectable vaccines, separate syringes and injection sites should be used. Use in Specific Populations: The safety and efficacy of PCV13 in pregnant women have not been established.
